title: Philosophy of Physics & Science
intro: Explore what quantum theory tells us about reality and how scientific knowledge works. Our reading group brings these questions together through three books.
meetingNote: Meeting dates, format, and pace will be announced by Prof. Leon.

sessions.title: The experiments a theory must explain
sessions.author: Tim Maudlin
sessions.description: Begin with the experimental starting point for our study of quantum interpretations. Keep a record of the phenomena an adequate interpretation needs to explain.
questions: Choose an experiment in the chapter. What is the setup, what is observed, and what needs explaining?
Which claims describe experimental results, and which claims propose an account of the reality behind those results?
What would you ask of an interpretation before accepting it as an adequate explanation?

sessions.title: What is the quantum world like?
sessions.author: Peter J. Lewis
sessions.description: After the Maudlin introduction, work through Lewis together. Compare the proposals we encounter by asking what exists on each view and how it accounts for the evidence.
questions: For the proposal under discussion, what does it say exists? State its central claim in your own words.
How does it account for the experiments we studied with Maudlin?
What is the strongest objection raised in the reading, and what reply is available?

sessions.title: How does science tell us about reality?
sessions.author: Peter Godfrey-Smith
sessions.assignment: Edition and chapter assignments to be confirmed
sessions.description: Work through the philosophy-of-science strand alongside our physics discussions. Use questions about evidence, explanation, and theory choice to connect the two strands.
questions: What picture of scientific knowledge is being proposed in the assigned reading?
What reasons does the author give for accepting or questioning that picture?
How might this discussion help us compare interpretations of quantum theory?
